text: The aforementioned studies, although providing interesting mechanistic insight into post-exercise nutritional responses, are limited to generating hypotheses regarding hypertrophic adaptations as opposed to drawing practical conclusions about the efficacy of nutrient timing for building muscle. Acute measures of muscle protein synthesis taken in the post-workout period are often decoupled from the chronic upregulation of causative myogenic signals (28) and do not necessarily predict long-term hypertrophic adaptations from regimented resistance training (136). In addition, post-workout elevations in muscle protein synthesis in untrained subjects are not replicated in those who are resistance trained (1).
